changes: Normalized the tithi spelling to 'pūrṇimā' and the weekday to 'Sunday (ravau)'.
Added notes: 'mahā…' may begin a title such as mahāmahopādhyāya, or may be the rest of a longer name, so 'Bhīma' may be incomplete.
Added notes: the scribe role rests only on the catalogue and the usual colophon formula, because the verb is lost in the lacuna. He could also be the commissioner or owner.
Added notes: LS conversion is not exact (+1118/1119) and Pauṣa falls around December–January, so the CE date is about 1542/43.
Persons, date (LS 424, about 1543 CE) and place (Kaṅkapura, not identified) otherwise kept as in the first reading.

notes: The colophon breaks off after 'miśraśrībhīmamahā' and the rest is lost (++++++++). 'mahā…' probably begins a title such as mahāmahopādhyāya, or may be part of a longer name, so 'Bhīma' may be incomplete. The verb is lost, so his role is not stated. Calling him the scribe follows the catalogue and the usual colophon pattern (place + name + likhitam), but he could also be the commissioner or owner. LS 424 + 1119 = 1543 CE. Because LS conversion is not exact and Pauṣa falls around December–January, the date is about 1542/43 CE. Kaṅkapura is not identified; it is presumably in Mithilā, since the script is Maithilī.
